short: MECOM, better known as EVI1, is a 145-kDa C2H2 zinc-finger protein with two separate finger clusters that bind two different sequences. The N-terminal cluster of seven fingers reads a 15-bp GATA-like site, GA(C/T)AAGA(T/C)AAGATAA, whose core is GACAAGATA; the C-terminal cluster of three fingers reads the unrelated GAAGATGAG. EVI1 is normally expressed in hematopoietic stem cells, kidney and lung, and is silenced in most differentiated blood cells. It is one of the strongest adverse prognostic markers in acute myeloid leukemia, where 3q26 rearrangements such as inv(3)(q21q26) do not create a fusion protein but move a GATA2 enhancer next to MECOM, switching the gene on. Germline MECOM mutations cause radioulnar synostosis with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.
long:
## The factors

MECOM (MDS1 and EVI1 complex locus, 3q26.2) encodes EVI1, first found as the site of retroviral
integration in murine myeloid leukemia cell lines. The protein carries two physically separate arrays of
Cys2-His2 zinc fingers, seven at the N terminus and three near the C terminus, plus a CtBP-interaction
motif and an acidic domain; it can act as a repressor or an activator depending on partners. A longer
read-through transcript, MDS1-EVI1, adds a PR/SET domain and is the reason EVI1 was once numbered
PRDM3. Unlike the PRDM family proper, the two finger clusters of EVI1 are used as independent
DNA-binding modules, which is why this atlas treats MECOM separately. EVI1 binds as a monomer, not an
obligate dimer, and one protein can engage both site types. Expression is restricted: hematopoietic stem
and progenitor cells, kidney, lung and developing heart and limb, with silencing on myeloid and
lymphoid differentiation. There is only one human gene, so there is no paralogue ambiguity within the
family, but there is considerable ambiguity with GATA factors.

## The motif

The proximal (N-terminal, fingers 1-7) cluster recognizes a 15-nucleotide consensus,
GA(C/T)AAGA(T/C)AAGATAA, which contains a tandem pair of GATA-like half-sites. Fingers 4-7 make the
sequence-specific contacts; fingers 1-3 do not detectably bind DNA on their own but bias the first
position toward GACAA over GATAA and are needed for optimal occupancy of the full 15-mer. The functional
minimal core is GACAAGATA, and a single amino-acid change (R205N) abolishes high-affinity binding to it.
Because GATAA is embedded in the site, EVI1 and GATA factors have overlapping but not identical
preferences: EVI1 binds erythroid GATA-1 target sites only weakly, while GATA-1 can bind and activate
through a GACAAGATAA element. The distal (C-terminal, three-finger) cluster binds a completely different
and shorter consensus, GAAGATGAG.

The database consensus in this atlas, TTATCTTATCT (and the 14-bp TATCTTATCWTATC archetype), is the
reverse complement of the proximal site written as tandem AGATAAGATAA half-sites; JASPAR renders the
same thing as AGATAAGATAA. So the literature consensus and the data agree once strand and finger cluster
are accounted for, and the longer Vierstra archetype simply captures more half-site repeats. No
widely used matrix in these databases represents the distal GAAGATGAG site, which is worth remembering:
scanning with a MECOM matrix tests only one of EVI1's two specificities.

## Where it acts

EVI1 occupancy in fibroblasts and myeloid cells maps to conserved GACAAGATA-like motifs within about
10 kb of transcription start sites of a defined target set, including GATA2, ZFPM2/FOG2, GADD45G, SKIL,
KLF5, DCN and MAP3K14. Sites are found in both promoters and distal elements. Because the proximal site
is a doubled GATA half-site, EVI1 peaks overlap GATA1/GATA2 peaks in hematopoietic cells, and in
erythroid or megakaryocytic chromatin a WGATAA-rich region is ambiguous between the two families. EVI1
also functions through protein interactions with a large partner network, including CtBP and
polycomb-associated proteins, so a fraction of its ChIP signal is likely tethered rather than
sequence-driven.

## Biology and disease

Conditional deletion of Evi1 in mice depletes hematopoietic stem cells and impairs repopulation, and
also blocks transformation by leukemic fusion oncogenes, making EVI1 required for both normal and
malignant stem-cell self-renewal. High EVI1 expression marks roughly 6-11% of adult acute myeloid
leukemia and is associated with poor outcome. The clearest mechanism is enhancer hijacking: in
inv(3)(q21q26) and t(3;3)(q21;q26), the breakpoint does not create a fusion protein but relocates a
distal GATA2 hematopoietic enhancer to the MECOM locus, driving EVI1 expression while leaving the
other GATA2 allele haploinsufficient. Two independent studies established this, one by mapping the
rearranged enhancer in patient genomes and one by deleting the orthologous mouse enhancer. Germline
biallelic or dominant MECOM mutations cause radioulnar synostosis with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia,
a bone-marrow-failure syndrome with a skeletal phenotype, confirming a developmental role beyond blood.

## Reading a hit

A MECOM match is a doubled GATA-like element, so the first alternative hypothesis is a GATA factor, not
EVI1 - especially in erythroid, megakaryocytic or endothelial cells where GATA1/GATA2 are abundant and
EVI1 is usually off. The 15-bp full site is long enough to be reasonably specific, but the shorter
matrices in these databases (10-11 bp, essentially two WGATAA half-sites) will match tandem GATA sites
indiscriminately. A hit on the distal GAAGATGAG specificity will not be found at all with the available
matrices. There is only one human MECOM gene, so a true EVI1 hit has no paralogue problem, but the
CIS-BP model is inferred from mouse Evi1 at 98% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured on the
human protein, and the Vierstra archetypes are named for MECOM without claiming separability from GATA.
Treat a hit as evidence for a GATA-type element and use expression data to decide whether EVI1 is a
plausible occupant.
caveats: The proximal EVI1 site is a tandem GATA-like element, so matches are shared with GATA1-GATA6 and TRPS1; in blood and endothelium a GATA factor is usually the more likely occupant, since EVI1 is off in most differentiated cells. The shorter matrices here are effectively two WGATAA half-sites and match tandem GATA sites indiscriminately. EVI1's second specificity, GAAGATGAG, is not represented by any matrix in these databases, so a MECOM scan tests only one of two binding modes. The CIS-BP model is inferred from mouse Evi1 (98% DBD identity), not measured on human EVI1. Part of EVI1's ChIP signal is likely tethered through its large protein-interaction network rather than direct.
